name: Canyon Creek
title: Window Cleaning in Canyon Creek Austin, TX | CleanzATX
description: Pure water window cleaning in Canyon Creek, Austin. Spot free glass from about $10 a window, $200 minimum, 7 day touch up. Quote by text from Tyler.
intro: Canyon Creek sits east of RM 620 near Boulder Lane, a large 1990s subdivision with greenbelt trails and its own elementary school. CleanzATX cleans the windows of homes here, with quotes by text from Tyler.

sections.h2: What Canyon Creek homes are like
paragraphs: Canyon Creek has roughly 1,000 homes, most of them 1990s production builds between about 2,000 and 3,500 square feet. Greenbelt trails run through the neighborhood, and Canyon Creek Elementary is part of the community. The Canyon Creek HOA oversees it, and there is no gate. The area is just outside the strict Four Points loop, but it is a short drive from our other work there.
Production homes from one builder tend to share layouts. That helps us quote accurately, because the window count on one street often matches the next.

sections.h2: What Canyon Creek windows deal with
paragraphs: Greenbelt means trees, and trees mean webs. Homes backing onto the trails get spiders working the corners of every frame, plus leaf litter in screens and tracks. Live oak pollen in March and April is heavy where the canopy is thick, and cedar pollen arrives in winter.

After thirty years, the glass has also seen a lot of sprinkler spray. Hard water spots on the lowest panes are common on homes this age, and some have been there long enough to need spot removal rather than a simple wash.

We approach Canyon Creek as a route of similar homes. Once we have cleaned one house on a street, the next goes faster because the layouts repeat. Exterior glass is done with pure water and poles from the ground, so back windows facing the greenbelt do not need a ladder. Screens that have collected webs and leaf bits can be cleaned the same day for $5 each. Many owners add a house soft wash because tree cover leaves green film on siding.
A 2,600 square foot home is about $260 for exterior windows and takes around two and a half hours. Inside and out at $15 a window would be near $390 for roughly 26 windows.

why: Greenbelt facing windows get webs and leaf debris cleared without ladders on slopes.
Similar 1990s layouts let us quote close to the final number by text.
Screens come off, get cleaned by hand and go back tight.
The 7 day touch up covers a missed spot at no charge.

faq.q: Why do my back windows get so many spider webs?
faq.a: Homes next to the greenbelt sit in the path of insects, and spiders follow. We brush webs off frames and corners as part of a window clean, which is easier on a regular schedule.

faq.q: Are you in Canyon Creek often?
faq.a: We work around Four Points regularly and schedule within two weeks in most cases. Texting your address and window count helps us place you near other jobs in this area.

faq.q: Do you pressure wash the house here?
faq.a: We soft wash siding and stucco instead, with a 12V system that is gentler on paint and mortar. Pricing begins at $0.20 per square foot, $400 minimum.

faq.q: What if I find a missed spot later?
faq.a: Text us a photo within 7 days. If we are in the area we come back and fix it free, and the job carries a 100% satisfaction guarantee.

faq.q: Can I get screens cleaned along with windows?
faq.a: Yes. Standard screens are $5, full screens $10, solar screens $15. On Triannual, Quarterly and Every 2 Months plans, a yearly screen cleaning is included.
